title: solve, explain, test, and analyze algorithm problems
concepts: A reliable solve process begins by restating the task as inputs, outputs, and a precise contract, then identifying constraints that rule algorithms in or out.
Clarifying questions should target ambiguity that changes correctness, such as empty input, duplicates, ordering, numeric limits, and whether mutation is allowed.
A small worked example exposes state changes, while a deliberately chosen edge case tests a boundary that the example may not reveal.
A brute-force baseline is useful for understanding the search space and building a correctness oracle, even when constraints require a faster final approach.
Choose data structures and algorithmic patterns from the required operations and input bounds; explain why a tempting alternative is too slow or violates an assumption.
State an invariant before optimizing code, then prove initialization, preservation, and termination; for recursive algorithms, include base cases and progress toward them.
Complexity analysis counts operations and stored state as functions of input size, distinguishing worst-case from expected and amortized claims where relevant.
A trustworthy final explanation connects problem contract, algorithm, correctness argument, complexity, implementation, and tests without claiming unverified behavior.
